claims.text: The initially solid Fe-Ni-Cr-Co-Cu nanoparticles are single-phase high-entropy alloys.
Limited atomic mobility governs the premelting and melting behavior of Fe-Ni-Cr-Co-Cu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Limited mobility permits stochastic local compositional fluctuations.
Local compositional fluctuations lead to transient duplex microstructures.
The transient duplex microstructures consist of precipitated or segregated element-rich regions.
Locally segregated regions have lower effective melting points than the homogeneous matrix.
Lower-melting segregated regions broaden the premelting regime relative to a fully homogenized nanoparticle.
The heterogeneous regions produce multi-step melting rather than a single sharp transition.
Rapid solidification favors limited mobility and local segregation in these nanoparticles.
Slow cooling minimizes local compositional fluctuations and produces a nearly homogeneous solid solution.
A slowly cooled, homogenized nanoparticle will exhibit a sharper and more uniform melting transition than a rapidly solidified nanoparticle.
Rapidly solidified nanoparticles will begin melting in locally segregated regions before the surrounding matrix.
Distinct thermal events during heating will correspond to the phases of the duplex microstructure.
Atomic mobility is inherently limited in high-entropy-alloy nanoparticle systems containing five or more elements.
The proposed mechanism is most relevant near the melting temperature.
The proposed mechanism may not apply when diffusion is rapid.
The proposed mechanism may not apply to larger particles whose melting behavior is bulk-dominated.
An absence of differences in melting onset, transition breadth, and duplex-microstructure development between rapidly and slowly cooled samples would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says compositional heterogeneity emerges during premelting because diffusion is restricted, whereas the predicted comparison attributes that heterogeneity primarily to prior rapid-solidification processing. The timing and origin of the proposed mediator are therefore ambiguous.
